subject: Electrical Engineering
title: The First Integrated Circuit: Kilby's Idea
description: A quick, practical guide to The First Integrated Circuit: Kilby's Idea.

hook.text: In 1958, Jack Kilby realized: why wire separate components when you can build them all on one chip?

buildup.text: He built transistors, resistors, and capacitors on a single germanium slab.

discovery.text: Robert Noyce independently created a silicon version with metal interconnects — more practical.

twist.text: Kilby won the Nobel Prize in 2000. Noyce, who died in 1990, did not — Nobels aren't posthumous.

climax.text: Their idea — the integrated circuit — became the foundation of the entire tech industry.

punchline.text: Put everything on one chip — the idea that built the modern world.

quiz.question: Who independently created a practical silicon integrated circuit?
